questions.q: What were this chapter's three confirmed root causes, in order?
options: A missing index, a batch job's open transaction blocking others, and parameter sniffing on a cached plan
Three separate missing indexes on three different tables
A single security misconfiguration affecting all three complaints
A failed backup, a failed restore, and a failed index rebuild
questions.explain: Billing's missing index, Scheduling's blocking transaction, and the later parameter sniffing bug were three genuinely distinct causes.

questions.q: Why did three different causes need three different fixes?
options: Each was a genuinely different mechanism — an index, a transaction boundary, and a plan-compilation behavior
Because Azure SQL Database requires a unique fix type for every ticket
They didn't — the same CREATE INDEX statement fixed all three
Only one of the three actually needed any fix at all
questions.explain: A missing index, prolonged locking, and parameter sniffing are mechanically unrelated problems, each requiring its own specific fix.

questions.q: What is the repeatable part of this chapter's approach?
options: The investigation method itself: sessions, slow queries, plan, diagnose, fix and re-test with proof
The exact table names dbo.Invoices and dbo.Appointments
The specific @ProviderID values used in the examples
The exact wording of the Billing and Scheduling emails
questions.explain: The five-step method generalizes to any real SQL Server or Azure SQL Database system, independent of this chapter's specific tables and bugs.

questions.q: Why do the monitoring dashboard and scheduled maintenance job still matter after all three bugs are fixed?
options: Maintenance that isn't automated quietly expires, and a future problem is more likely to show up as a dashboard row than a new complaint
They are purely optional and have no effect once the bugs are resolved
They are required only during the initial Beginner-project backup work
They automatically rewrite stored procedures to prevent parameter sniffing
questions.explain: Lessons 11 and 12 are what keep the fixes from silently degrading and catch future problems proactively instead of reactively.

questions.q: What does the Advanced project focus on, compared to this Intermediate project?
options: Architecture, resilience, and platform-level decisions that reduce how often problems like these occur in the first place, beyond one database
Repeating the exact same three fixes on a second identical database
Returning to backup and restore work from the Beginner project
Replacing Azure SQL Database with an entirely different platform
questions.explain: This project diagnosed and fixed problems after they happened; the Advanced project goes further into reducing their occurrence at a larger scale.
